design.title: World-axis relational geometry with finite-wall face coordinates
design.coverage_gap: The exact five-episode support contains three LL and two HH layouts and no LH/HL layouts. Object-to-goal lateral displacements in support are small, so raw independent absolute coordinates may encourage a same-side shortcut. Extrapolation also widens hand-to-object error beyond these demonstrations.
design.reusable_regularity: Represent approach by object minus hand, transport by goal minus object/hand, and obstruction by signed coordinates relative to all six faces of the finite axis-aligned wall. Native gravity and world axes remain explicit. Physical scales, rather than per-edge support standard deviations, keep previously tiny lateral goal errors numerically meaningful without huge off-support normalization. This is a representation bias only: the common U-Net learns the action sequence without hand-coded waypoints or control corrections.
dependencies_preserved: Hand, object and goal world locations are reconstructible from wall center and relative vectors; absolute z channels preserve table/gravity dependence.
Wall center and all three half sizes are retained, including its asymmetric finite x footprint; it is not replaced with an infinite barrier or removed through translation invariance.
Current and native-previous object xyzw quaternions, aperture, aperture change, hand/object displacements and relative slip are retained. Absent object2 zero channels are omitted.
Two whole causal observations are independently represented, including the previous fields inside each observation. No episode time or phase oracle is used.

evidence_refs.use: Defines the exact D5 evidence scope and episode identities.
World-coordinate field slices, action4 semantics, diagonal training cells and finite wall channels.

LL=3, HH=2; initial goal-object x differences roughly -0.006 to 0.005 m; wall center (0.10,0.75,0.06) and half sizes (0.12,0.01,0.06). These motivate relations but not deletion of absolute obstacle geometry.
Inspected actual frame: object below hand, finite wall between approach side and goal side.
Aperture closure and relative hand/object motion distinguish approach from lift without a clock; actions change from downward approach to vertical lift.
Factory, causal observation and immutable common action-loss requirements.

expected_failure_signature: If explicit relations alone do not resolve the diagonal shortcut, grasping may generalize while object-goal lateral residual remains large in LH/HL and extrapolated opposite-side cells.
A single ungated denoiser may confuse late descent with early approach, or translate before lifting. Such errors should appear as low wall clearance or object-hand separation after closure.
The representation does not impose rotation equivariance or a collision-free planner; failures at finite wall edges would falsify the sufficiency of face features.

required_runtime_fields.source: causal_context.raw_history [B,2,45], identical shared observations; normalized history is intentionally not used
required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Identity native world_dx, world_dy, world_dz, gripper at all sixteen chunk positions. Native xyz unit is 0.01 m. Candidate performs no action clipping; public executor alone clips world action4 and executes four actions.

design.support_fit: No fitted statistics or learned modules beyond the factory DP. Fixed dimensional scales are declared in config; no other data are used.
design.change_summary: Initial A1: fixed world-axis edge and wall-face representation, no auxiliary loss, no encoder, no action-frame change. No structural repairs at authorship.
